title: Do bias mechanisms in an unanchored MAIC combine additively?
question: When an omitted confounder, comparator outcome misclassification and covariate measurement error act together on an unanchored MAIC, is their joint bias the sum of their separate biases, and does a one-at-a-time analysis bound it?
design: Population-level numerical study: exact bias of the MAIC limit over 45 combinations of three mechanisms, with interaction terms by inclusion-exclusion.
answer: No. An omitted confounder and misclassification of the comparator's outcome interacted by up to 0.16 on the log odds ratio scale: with both at their largest the joint bias was about half the sum of the separate biases, and with the confounder reversed the joint bias had the opposite sign to that sum. Measurement error in a matched covariate combined nearly additively with either. The joint bias exceeded the largest single-mechanism bias in 22 of 36 combinations, so one-at-a-time analyses neither add up to nor bound it.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: median interaction 30% of the summed separate biases where two or three mechanisms acted.
Confounder by misclassification: interaction up to 0.163; other pairs at most 0.005.
Joint bias beyond the largest single-mechanism bias in 22 of 36 combinations; mechanisms partly cancelled in 16.
not_answered: Population-level only; no bias-analysis procedure, false reassurance or tipping sets; three mechanisms; selection and correlated parameters not varied. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Marginal log odds ratio, B versus A, in the target (unanchored)
methods_compared: unanchored MAIC limit under combinations of three bias mechanisms
